newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Forbes mulls listing to raise cash.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Forbes mulls listing to raise cash.

text.p: South African financial services and insurance group Forbes Financial Services said on Thursday a public listing would enable the company to raise the cash necessary for growth.

Forbes said last month it was considering listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. No firm decision had yet been taken on the timing or details of the proposed listing in the bourse's insurance sector.
"Our businesses have been involved in a lot of deals recently and we need the cash for growth," said Paul Heinamann, group chairman and managing director.
"We have to respond to the needs of our own companies," Heinamann said.
Although there were still growth opportunities in South Africa, Forbes was also looking at further expansion internationally.
"We still see growth locally but we have become too big to only focus on South Africa," he said.

Forbes is already active offshore through its stake in U.K and European risk management, financial services and insurance broking group, Nelson Hurst plc. The group has a network of offices in Latin America and Asia.
Heinamann said Nelson Hurst would continue to seek opportunities in emerging markets.

Forbes, which is 70 percent owned by leisure group Servgro International Ltd, said last month it had lifted attributable profit 31 percent to 55 million rand in the 1996 financial year. It said it expected further growth from its divisions.

The Forbes group includes Alexander Forbes Consultants and Actuaries, an employee benefits firm, Price Forbes, a short-term insurance, broking and risk management operation and Forbes Reinsurance Broking Services, the largest South African reinsurance broker.
